- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to counteract overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price peaks in late period (last 7–10 days); apply +0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., -0.5 to +0.5 within 3 days), model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to capture sentiment shift.
